title: Leen — AI Operating System
summary: An AI operating environment for agents, durable workflows, memory, integrations, and governed execution — the platform I co-founded and lead as CTO.
contributionSummary: Co-founded the platform and serve as CTO. Scope spans platform boundaries, core subsystem design, and engineering leadership. Delivery is a team effort — solo ownership of the full stack is not claimed.
maturityNotice: Leen is in active development. This page describes the platform direction and my role; it is not presented as a commercially launched product.

sections.title: What Leen is
paragraphs: Leen (formerly Muazaf) is an AI operating environment — a platform for building and running intelligent business systems. The direction combines conversational copilots, durable workflow execution, agent runtimes, shared memory, and governed integrations into one coherent stack.
The goal is not a single chatbot or automation script. It is an operating layer where business operations can be expressed, executed, and evolved with appropriate controls.

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: Teams adopting AI often end up with disconnected tools: a copilot here, a webhook automation there, brittle prompts with no memory, and no clear boundary between experimentation and production execution.
Leen addresses the platform gap — giving operators a structured environment for agents, workflows, and integrations rather than one-off AI features.
bullets: Fragmented AI tooling that does not compose into durable systems
Workflow logic that breaks when context or channels change
Lack of governance over what agents can access and execute

sections.title: Platform architecture
paragraphs: The platform is organized as a set of core systems that compose together. Each area below is a major boundary in the architecture — not a separate product silo.

subsections.title: Copilot
items: Conversational interface layer for operators and business users

subsections.title: Workflows
items: Durable workflow engine for multi-step, governed automation

subsections.title: Agent Runtime
items: Execution environment for agent tasks and tool use

subsections.title: Teams
items: Multi-actor coordination and role boundaries within the platform

subsections.title: Memory
items: Persistent context and knowledge retention across sessions

subsections.title: Business Solutions
items: Vertical and operational solution patterns built on platform primitives

subsections.title: Apps Platform

subsections.title: Governance and Security

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: As Co-Founder and CTO, I lead platform direction, architectural boundaries, and core engineering decisions. Work spans subsystem design, integration strategy, and hands-on implementation across the stack.
Team contribution exists across the platform. This page does not imply solo delivery of every subsystem.

sections.title: Key engineering decisions
paragraphs: The platform prioritizes composable primitives over monolithic features — agents, workflows, and memory are first-class boundaries rather than bolt-ons.
Governed execution is treated as a platform concern, not an afterthought in individual features.
bullets: Separate conversational, workflow, and agent layers with explicit integration contracts
Earlier Muazaf support-platform work preceded and informed this direction

sections.title: Current status and lessons
paragraphs: Leen is in active development. Engineering continues across core subsystems. This is not presented as a commercially launched product.
Earlier Muazaf support-platform work (see the Omnichannel case study) came first; after that effort, work shifted to this broader platform direction.
bullets: Platform thinking early prevents expensive rework when AI features multiply
Clear contribution boundaries matter as team scale grows

decisions.title: Platform primitives over feature silos
decisions.context: AI capabilities were accumulating as isolated features without shared execution or memory boundaries.
decisions.decision: Organize the platform around composable primitives — copilot, workflows, agents, memory, and governance — with explicit integration contracts.
decisions.tradeoff: Higher upfront architectural investment; clearer long-term evolution and less duplication.
